transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in today?

Yeah, thanks, Doctor. I guess what’s bringing me in is… I’ve been having a hard time staying locked in when I need to. Like at work, I can start a safety briefing or go over a plan and I’m really trying to pay attention, but a few minutes in my mind’s already jumped to three other job problems.

And then I realize I missed something I probably should’ve caught. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but it’s been happening enough that I figured I should talk to someone about it.
Has this kind of trouble staying focused been something you've dealt with since childhood or your school years, or is this a new change for you?

Yeah… it’s not totally new. I mean, I don’t want to blame everything on when I was a kid, but back in elementary school, teachers were already telling my parents stuff like I couldn’t stay in my seat, I’d talk out of turn, lose homework, and rush through directions before I really understood what I was supposed to do.

I guess I always hoped I’d just grow out of it, or learn to manage it better. Does that kind of answer what you mean?
When your mind jumps to those other job problems, does it feel more like uncontrollable worry or anxiety about them, or just your attention drifting without any particular worry attached?

I’d say it’s more my attention drifting than, like, panic or worry. I mean, the job problems are real things I have to handle, but in those moments I’m not sitting there scared about them exactly. I’ll be trying to follow a safety briefing or a plan review, and within a few minutes my brain is already off on three other things, and then I realize I missed something I should’ve caught.

I hope that makes sense. It’s not that I’m not trying to listen.
These days, do you still notice things like feeling restless, needing to move around, or acting or speaking impulsively before thinking things through?

Yeah… I mean, I try not to, especially at work, but I do catch myself cutting people off sometimes. Like I’ll think I already know where their question is going, so I jump in and answer too fast.

Then halfway through, or after they finish, I realize there was an important part they hadn’t even said yet. It’s not like I’m trying to be rude… I just get ahead of it. I don’t know if that’s the kind of thing you mean.
Do you notice this same kind of difficulty focusing or acting impulsively in other parts of your life outside of work, like at home or with family and friends?

Yeah… I mean, I wish I could say it was just work, but it does show up at home too.

Like, my wife has to remind me about things I told her I’d take care of, and I know that wears on her. I don’t mean to leave it on her, but I’ll say I’m going to handle something and then it just… doesn’t happen unless she brings it up again.

And at work, honestly, it’s gotten to the point where missed follow-ups and messy coordination on site have led to my employer raising concerns. I’m not proud of that. I try to stay on top of things, but it’s been affecting more than one area, if that’s what you’re asking.

Have you noticed any recent changes in your mood, sleep, or energy levels—like feeling unusually elevated, depressed, or using alcohol or other substances—that might be contributing to these focus and impulsivity issues?

I don’t think so… not that I’ve noticed, anyway. My mood’s been pretty normal, I guess—maybe frustrated with myself, but not like unusually up or down.

Sleep and energy… I mean, they’re not perfect, but I wouldn’t say there’s been some big recent change that explains it. And I’m not using anything like that. Alcohol isn’t really something I’d point to as the cause.

I don’t know if that answers it the way you’re asking, but I don’t think there’s been some separate mood or substance thing driving this.
Have these attention and impulsivity difficulties—at work and at home—been going on consistently for the past six months or more, or have they been more sporadic?

It’s been more consistent, yeah. I’d like to say it’s just been here and there, but… it’s been going on a while.

The part where it’s really started disrupting my job has been about two years now—maybe a little over two years, like two years and a couple months. It seemed to get a lot harder after the construction schedule changed and the hours got more chaotic.

At home too, it’s not brand new. I guess I just kept thinking I could get it under control, but it hasn’t really gone away. Does that answer what you mean?
Do you often find yourself losing or misplacing things you need, like tools, paperwork, or your phone, or forgetting appointments and commitments even when you try to keep track of them?

Yeah… I mean, I try to keep track of things, but I do misplace stuff a lot.

I’m kind of always patting my pockets or digging through the truck looking for my keys, or my tape, or my notebook. Sometimes it’s the marked-up drawings I need, and then I’m holding everyone up trying to find them. Even my phone—I’ll swear I just had it in my hand, and then it’s gone.

I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but… yeah, it happens enough that it’s a problem. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
